subject: general
question: Who predicted 'nuclear technology is going to be very essential and not just in the power sector but for other societal uses intended for betterment of life'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Homi J Bhabha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Homi J Bhabha, the founder of India's nuclear programme**, predicted that "nuclear technology will be highly important not only in the power industry but also for various societal uses aimed at improving life."
 
• **India's nuclear programme dates back to March 1944,** and its three-stage technological efforts were formed by Homi Jehangir Bhabha when he built the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research, a nuclear research centre. 
 
• In **1956**, India developed its first research reactor, and by 1964, it had completed its first plutonium reprocessing unit.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Homi Jehangir Bhabha **was an Indian nuclear scientist, founder of the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research, and professor of physics (TIFR). Bhabha was the founding director of the Atomic Energy Establishment, Trombay (AEET), which is now known as the Bhabha Atomic Research Centre in his honour.
 
• He is also recognised as the **"Father of the Indian Nuclear Program."** TIFR and AEET were the cornerstones of India's nuclear weapons development, which Bhabha oversaw as director.
 
• **Avul Pakir Jainulabdeen Abdul Kalam **was the 11th President of India, serving from 2002 to 2007.
 
• **Sir Jagadish Chandra Bose** was a major force behind the expansion of experimental science on the Indian subcontinent. He pioneered the investigation of radio and microwave optics, made significant contributions to plant science, and was a major force behind the expansion of experimental science on the Indian subcontinent.
 
• **Sir Chandrasekhara Venkata Raman **was an Indian physicist who pioneered light scattering research.
